reforms.description: In response to identified weaknesses in basic research and the 'hollowing-out' of Japan's R&D, the Japanese government adopted a five-year plan in July 1996 to improve the quality of R&D and increase public spending on basic research. This initiative aligns with OECD recommendations to increase emphasis on basic research and improve efficiency of public spending on technology, with the goal of laying the foundation for future innovation through numerous government initiatives across public, private and university sectors.
reforms.component_name: Technology and Innovation — Basic Research Emphasis
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased public investment in basic research strengthens the knowledge foundation for future technological innovation and productivity growth, addressing a structural weakness in Japan's innovation system.
reforms.status_evidence: Five-year plan adopted by Japanese government in July 1996 with government initiatives already underway across sectors.
reforms.importance_rationale: A five-year government plan to systematically increase public R&D spending and improve research quality across multiple sectors represents a structural, system-wide policy change.
reforms.source_quote: Increase the emphasis on basic research and improve the efficiency of public spending on technology. While Japan has had remarkable success in technology development, basic research will help lay the foundation for future innovation.

reforms.description: Japan's revised New Business Law, applicable to unlisted venture companies, allows advantageous issuance of new stock (up to one-third of total shares) to directors and employees within ten years of a special shareholder agreement. By August 1996, only 57 companies had been certified by MITI under this scheme.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Facilitating equity issuance for venture company employees and directors reduces capital constraints and incentive misalignment in early-stage innovative firms, supporting commercialization and entrepreneurship.
reforms.status_evidence: Revised New Business Law was applicable by 1996, with 57 companies certified by MITI by August 1996.
reforms.importance_rationale: A legislative reform to the New Business Law represents a significant but narrower policy change focused on venture capital structure rather than a system-wide overhaul.
reforms.source_quote: The revised New Business Law is only applicable to unlisted venture companies. By August 1996, only 57 companies had been certified by MITI. It allows an advantageous issue of new stock, amounting to as much as a third of total shares, to both directors and employees within ten years of a special agreement at a general shareholders meeting.

reforms.description: The 1995 'New Sunshine Programme' focuses on energy conservation research, representing a sectoral R&D initiative targeting a specific policy priority in the energy sector.
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted energy conservation research supports long-term productivity and competitiveness in a strategically important sector while addressing environmental sustainability.
reforms.status_evidence: The New Sunshine Programme was in operation by 1995.
reforms.importance_rationale: A sectoral R&D programme targeting energy conservation represents a significant but focused initiative rather than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The 1995 'New Sunshine Programme', for example, focuses on energy conservation.

reforms.description: The 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasises research in new materials, biotechnology and information technologies, representing a multi-sectoral R&D initiative addressing emerging technology domains.
reforms.component_name: Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Targeted investment in high-impact technology domains (materials, biotechnology, IT) supports innovation capacity and future competitiveness in strategically important sectors.
reforms.status_evidence: The text describes the programme without explicit evidence of implementation; status inferred as announced pending further evidence.
reforms.importance_rationale: A multi-sectoral R&D programme targeting emerging technologies represents a significant but focused initiative rather than a system-wide reform.
reforms.source_quote: The 'Industrial Science and Technology Frontier Programme' emphasises new materials, biotechnology and information technologies.
